wrist_mount.note: PincOpen assembly frame -> robot frame at the arm ZERO pose. APPROXIMATE, derived from the stock gripper: +X = the arm_wrist_roll axis (0,0.42262,-0.90631) = the stock finger direction; +Z = -arm_gripper hinge axis (0,0.90631,0.42262) so the PincOpen camera stack points the same way as the stock Wrist-Camera-Mount-v11; +Y = Z x X = robot -X = the stock jaw opening direction. Origin: the PincOpen back face (full-gripper X_min = -53.49 mm) is put on the wrist-roll output flange (the stock Wrist_Roll_08c-v1 bracket starts 1.0 mm behind it) and the PincOpen mirror plane Y=0 and finger mid-plane Z=0 are put on the stock gripper centreline. Assumed: PincOpen bolts straight onto the wrist-roll flange with no adapter plate; no CAD of the real adapter was available. Expect a few mm of error along +X.

pose.note: camera <- Camera-Model-v3 link frame (mm), column-major: col0 = image right, col1 = image up, col2 = -optical axis, col3 = sensor point. Derived from the URDF visual origin of the link (xyz -0.01601 0.00243 -0.01139, rpy 1.74533 1.39626 -pi) plus meshes/Camera-Model-v3.stl: a 38x38x3 mm board at mesh z 0..3 with an M12 lens barrel (r 6.1..6.8) from z 3 to 21.5, so the optical axis is mesh +Z and the sensor is the board front face, mesh (0,0,3). At the base pose that is robot (0, 111.75, 25.05) aiming (0, 0.98481, 0.17365) = +Y, 10.000 deg ABOVE horizontal (verified: the axis ray clears Camera-Mount-v8 and every stock mesh, never meets the ground, and matches docs/analysis/real_front.png). robot_matrix is the same pose already multiplied through FK, used when ctx.fk cannot resolve the link.

hfov_source.what: Arducam 5MP OV5648 wide-angle USB camera (B0972/UB0233), the LeKiwi BOM's camera option: 'Field of View (FOV): 90 degree (H)', M12 lens. external/LeKiwi/BOM.md footnote 2 + 3DPrinting.md name this camera for base_camera_mount.stl, and the URDF's Camera-Model-v3 is that 38 mm board camera (not the clip-on Vinmooog webcam listed on the same BOM line).

hfov_alternatives.label: 110 deg DFOV variant
hfov_alternatives.note: Arducam B0454 '5MP OV5648, 110 Degree DFOV Wide Angle' - 110 deg diagonal on a rectilinear 4:3 frame = 97.7 deg H / 81.3 deg V.

hfov_alternatives.label: cover.py assumption
hfov_alternatives.note: This repo's scripts/cover.py (2026-08) assumed a '90 deg diagonal lens = +/-33 h, +/-25 v'. Conservative; kept so the old coverage numbers can be reproduced.

pose.note: world = FK(Wrist_Roll_08c-v1) . frames.wrist_mount.local . frameToMatrix(frames.cam_wrist). frames.cam_wrist comes from wrist_cam_mount.build() in the PincOpen assembly frame (+X fingertip direction, Y=0 mirror plane); at the default +22 variant the head is 25+22 = 47 deg nose-down. The fallback is that same shipped NormaCam +22 datum, used when the part is not built.

hfov_source.what: Fitted, not a datasheet: studio/docs/analysis/wrist.py least-squares three landmarks in the REAL wrist feed (servo LED, gripper body top edge, fingertip) for tilt + half-vertical FOV and gets 32.7 deg half-vFOV, i.e. 65.4 deg V = 81 deg H at 4:3. wrist_cam_mount.build() publishes the same 81 in frames.cam_wrist.hfov_deg, which wins over this default until the user edits it.

pose.note: mast_upper.build().frames.cam_top, already in the robot frame: {origin, tilt_deg, dir = (0, cos t, -sin t)} with tilt_deg the nose-down angle. Falls back to profile frames.cam_top_rev8 (0, 25, 387.1) tilt 65 = the head as printed.

hfov_source.what: Fitted, not a datasheet: studio/docs/analysis/README.md + fit.py fit the two front omni wheels in a screenshot of the live top feed and get hFOV 58-62 deg (4:3 -> ~46 deg V). The same fit says the INSTALLED head aims ~71 deg down against a 65 deg design, i.e. ~6 deg of droop. mast_upper.build() publishes 60 in frames.cam_top.hfov_deg.

joint_limits_note: Source: TheRobotStudio/SO-ARM100, Simulation/SO101/so101_new_calib.urdf (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheRobotStudio/SO-ARM100/main/Simulation/SO101/so101_new_calib.urdf, fetched 2026-09-12) -- the only SO-101 description that carries <limit> tags. Its <limit> values, in degrees: shoulder_pan +-110, shoulder_lift +-100, elbow_flex +-96.83, wrist_flex +-95, wrist_roll -157.21..+162.79, gripper -10..+100. The LeKiwi URDF (external/LeKiwi/URDF/LeKiwi.urdf) has NO <limit> tags and, more importantly, a DIFFERENT joint zero: its zero pose is the folded/parked CAD configuration (upper arm horizontal backwards, forearm folded forward again) while the reference zero has the upper arm up and the forearm forward. The mapping q_lekiwi = sign * q_ref + offset_deg was solved geometrically, not guessed: both URDFs describe the same physical arm, so for each joint the axis LINE (point + direction) of every downstream joint must coincide once the two chains are aligned by one rigid transform. Fitting sign+offset per joint over 6-8 random configurations leaves max axis-line offset 5.1 mm and max axis-angle 0.87 deg (identity mapping: 254 mm / 180 deg; the best wrong sign combination: 145x worse cost), the residual being the genuine CAD difference between the two exports (forearm 136.0 vs 135.0 mm, two DH offsets 1.5 and 3.5 mm apart). Signs: pan +1, lift/elbow/wrist_flex/wrist_roll/gripper -1 -- i.e. every LeKiwi arm axis except the shoulder pan points the opposite way to the SO-101 reference axis. The pan offset is not observable from geometry (a base rotation absorbs it) and is taken as 0, which is correct by inspection: at pan 0 the arm points robot +Y in both models, and the limit is symmetric anyway. The gripper offset is likewise not observable from the axis lines (nothing is downstream of it), and a mesh test cannot find it either: the stock jaw pivots INSIDE its own bracket, so Moving_Jaw_08d-v1 intersects Wrist_Roll_08c-v1 at every angle from -120 to +103 deg in the decimated meshes. It is taken as 0 on the finger-tip measurement instead: tip separation (moving-jaw tip to fixed-finger tip, collide.js gripOpening) falls monotonically 142.2 mm at -100, 62.7 at -30, 41.6 at -15, 20.1 at 0, 7.1 at +10, with its minimum 6.2 mm at +15 -- so LeKiwi arm_gripper 0 is the near-closed jaw exactly as the reference's 0 is, +10 is the closed stop (matching the reference's 10 deg of over-close) and NEGATIVE arm_gripper OPENS. This also agrees with the app's own presets, which use arm_gripper -30 for the two reaching poses. SANITY: the LeKiwi URDF zero pose (all six joints 0) lands inside every one of these ranges, 3.8..69.3 deg from the nearest stop -- as a parked CAD pose should. CAVEAT for the app: three of the four presets shipped in docs/VERIFY.md were authored before any limit existed and fall OUTSIDE this range -- stowed (lift +40, wrist_flex -54), reach floor (lift +20, elbow -76), reach table (lift +9). Only 'raised max' is legal. Independently of the limits, collide.js finds those same three presets to be in HARD COLLISION with the robot (upper arm through Base_08q / the WaveShare plate / the deck plate), so they are not merely out of travel, they are impossible. See studio/docs/MOTION.md for IK-corrected replacements that hit the same tip positions. arm_joint_range_deg above is the OLD UI travel hint and is kept only so that nothing that reads it breaks; joint_limits_deg is the physical one.
